_README: Pinned material map for office_room.obj. Keys are the OBJ's usemtl group names; values encode the reflectance/transmittance the names carry (R020 -> refl 0.20, T073 -> glass tvis 0.73, etc.). An on-disk map that covers every group wins over the tester's auto-generated map, so these EXACT values are used (the auto-map would otherwise default glazing to tvis 0.65 and mis-type Rad_ScreenGlass as a window). units/up_axis/north_angle_deg are read alongside the group specs. This Blender export is Z-up (height on +Z), so up_axis is Z. ORIENTATION (re-authored 2026-07-05): the geometry is now modelled directly in the true-north frame, so north_angle_deg is 0. The single window sits in the wall named South (model -Y), so at north_angle_deg 0 it is a SOUTH-facing window (its outward -Y normal points true south). This mirrors the compass-named materials in radiance/materials.rad. Rad_Luminaire_L09 is type:luminaire bound to the L09_neutral fixture (IES photometry + measured SPD) so import_geometry returns a drop-in electric_lights payload for run_grid/run_image; the ies/spd are ABSOLUTE paths so import_geometry(sidecar=...) resolves them irrespective of cwd (edit if you relocate the repo or swap CCT L09_warm/L09_cool). NOTE: the pre-authored radiance/office_room.rad scene is the equivalent hand-built path (materials in radiance/materials.rad, IES emitters in radiance/luminaires_L09.rad).
